source.author: Jitsuro Nagura
source.title: On The Interval Containing At Least One Prime Number
source.journal: Proceedings of the Japan Academy, volume 28, issue 4, pages 177–181 (1952)
source.statement_location: page 177, opening paragraph; visually read on the pinned PDF first page
source.exact_observed_wording: within which at least one prime number exists; this paper, however, enables us to reduce it up to between x and 6x/5 where x ≥ 25
source.imported_statement: For every real x>=25 there exists a prime p with x<p<6x/5. The candidate uses only positive integer x=floor(n/2)>=25; if the wording 'between' were read as allowing the upper endpoint, that endpoint cannot be prime for integer x>=25 because an integral 6x/5 is a multiple of 6. The lower endpoint is used strictly.
source.proof_status: The primary statement and source metadata were read; Nagura's proof was NOT reconstructed, replayed, independently reviewed or formally checked. Public PDF text extraction was incomplete, so the first page was read as an image.
